rationale: A direct public Yuku TSRX parse-to-output control reaches 129.73 MiB/s on the read-only Markless corpus, about 10.45x the previously measured full JavaScript AST decode/re-encode path and 8.65x the final 15 MiB/s gate. It reparses, preserves normalized semantics and comments, is idempotent, and handles the retained BigInt source. However, the unmodified Yuku code generator is not a configuration-compatible formatter: 119/178 outputs retain leading tabs under useTabs:false and 57/178 exceed printWidth 100, including a breakable 288-column line. The approved architecture therefore pins the public MIT TSRX parser revision as a build dependency, keeps its indexed tree entirely native, adds a repository-owned format-oriented layout layer behind one N-API call, and preserves the T007 fallback plus direct official Oxfmt standard-file path. No OXC source, private API, or downstream patch queue is introduced.
